trial_court: Court of District Judge, Indore in Hindu Marriage Case No. 47/90
case_name: Gunuveena Singh vs Capt. Pankaj Puneet Singh
facts_of_case: Marriage between parties was solemnized on 14-4-87. Respondent treated appellant with cruelty and deserted her in Oct. 1988. Appellant claimed restoration of property retained by respondent.

legal_principles.principle: The law must provide a protective umbrella to free the petitioner from the boneful bond of marriage which gave only tears and torture.
legal_principles.held: Such attitude of the husband is palpably irremissible. The husband can have neither vote nor veto.
use_in: divorce cases involving cruelty and desertion

legal_principles.principle: The court must scrutinise as to who has wronged and who is wronged.
legal_principles.held: The Court, acting reasonably and judiciously, is obligated to scrutinise...
use_in: cases involving disputes over wrongs committed

legal_principles.principle: The law must not stay petrified in matters of mental cruelty.
legal_principles.held: Must the cause perish in law on sheer technicalities or military-like insistence on pleadings?
use_in: cases involving claims of mental cruelty

outcome.final_order: Trial Court dismissed the petition seeking dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

use_for_drafting: responding to summons in divorce case
claiming property retention in divorce proceedings
